result.summary: Introduces multiprocess capabilities to Bitcoin Core by adding an --enable-multiprocess build option and IPC support using Cap'n Proto. It enables bitcoin-gui and bitcoin-node to spawn isolated subprocesses and communicate across socket pairs via the Init, Node, and Wallet interfaces. It also updates btcsignals to destroy disconnected callbacks eagerly and includes libmultiprocess subtree updates.
result.problem: Running the node, GUI, and wallet within a single monolithic process means a crash, vulnerability, or high resource utilization in the GUI or wallet can compromise the entire node. Separating them into isolated processes improves security and stability while enabling independent lifecycles.

resolved_concerns: Replaced Boost signals with btcsignals eager destruction to resolve shutdown hangs
Added atomic shared_ptr fallback for platforms missing full C++20 standard library support
Resolved logging clashing by appending process-specific log suffixes (.gui and .wallet)

result.card: This PR provides the primary implementation of multiprocess Bitcoin Core, allowing the node, GUI, and wallet to run in distinct processes communicating over socket pairs via Cap'n Proto. It solves monolithic coupling, protecting the daemon from GUI and wallet crashes or vulnerabilities. It is the flagship PR of the process separation project (#28722) and has wide Concept ACK support from maintainers. Code review is actionable now, though reviewers should start with base PR #29409 upon which this rests.
